question: Pick a piece of text in a short window and its own settings are off the bottom of the panel. What should give?
context: The dock is asked for about 1090 points of sections in a 688 point panel, so something has to be below the fold. Measured on the probe at 1200 by 720 with a marked-up screenshot: Layers, Appearance, Effects, Measurements fill the panel and the Text section starts 72 points past the bottom edge. Same at 1200 by 960. Two of your own asks collide here: put what you picked first (6 September) and Appearance and Effects directly under Layers (7 September).

options.label: What you picked goes above Effects
options.summary: The panel reads Layers, Appearance, then the section named after the thing you picked, then Effects. Pick a piece of text and its Style, Font, Size, Weight and alignment rows are all on screen; Effects starts right under them and you scroll for its sliders.
pros: The settings for the thing you just clicked are always whole on screen, at every window size tried
Opacity and Fill stay directly under Layers, one glance from the list, which is what you asked for on 7 September
Effects keeps its heading on screen, so you can always see it is there and open it
cons: When a layer carries an open shadow, the shadow sliders are below the fold and need a short scroll
options.mitigation: Effects is a list you scroll inside anyway once it holds more than one effect, so the scroll is one you already do; its heading and its plus button stay in place.

options.label: What you picked goes first, above everything
options.summary: The panel reads Layers, then the section named after the thing you picked, then Appearance, then Effects. The strongest version of put what you picked first: click text and the text settings are the very next thing under the list.
pros: What you clicked is unmissable, right under the row you clicked
The picked settings are whole on screen at every window size
cons: Opacity and Fill move down by the height of a whole section, so on a plain rectangle they sit lower than they do today
Where Opacity lives now depends on what you picked, so it moves around as you click between layers
options.mitigation: For a plain shape nothing changes at all, since a rectangle has no section of its own.

options.label: Leave the panel as it is
options.summary: Appearance and Effects stay directly under Layers. In a short window, picking text or a zoom callout leaves its own settings off the bottom of the panel with no heading showing, and you scroll down to find them.
pros: Nothing moves; Opacity, Fill and the effects list stay exactly where you put them on 7 September
cons: Pick a piece of text in a 720 point tall window and there is nothing on screen saying text settings exist at all
This is the same thing you asked to have fixed on 6 September, back again from the other direction
options.mitigation: In a tall window the settings do fit, so this only bites when the window is short.

answer.note: Style, font size, weight, etc are all appearance settings and belong in the appearance pane
